phase2.title: Phase 2: analysis code skeleton and ideas list

phase1.verdict_context: This is the second pass, after network access was opened. I read every Toronto open-data record through the City's open-data API and downloaded and profiled the files. I also fetched the City of Toronto, CMHC and OLT pages and pulled CMHC tables directly. StatCan (HTTP 403/503) and the Ontario legislature and e-Laws pages (403, or script-rendered) still could not be read, so claims that depend on them are marked UNVERIFIED.
phase1.prepared_note: Prepared 2026-10-30. The study is descriptive and associational; nothing here supports causal claims.

limitations.body: CMHC returns census-tract completions for 2010–2022. Exports for 2023 onward say "This data series is now archived". Toronto-wide completions continue to 2025, and census-tract starts continue to 2025. The census tracts reconcile with the city total (16,292 vs. 16,296 in 2022).

limitations.lead: Zoning history is only partly recoverable.
sub: The open zoning layer is one snapshot, "updated to include amendments up to June 18th, 2023".
Backcasting is possible for 569-2013 lands: 27.5% of 5,247 Chapter 900 exceptions cite their amending by-law with its year. The Wayback Machine also holds copies from 2023-04 and 2024-06.
Lands still under former by-laws have no GIS. That covers 50.8% of 50+ unit new-building permit sites.

limitations.lead: 569-2013 did not fully replace the former by-laws.
limitations.body: The City says it "does not fully replace all older bylaws in every area". About 1,500 low-rise parcels were excluded, and 2026 by-laws are still bringing lands in. Some 2013 provisions remain under OLT appeal (PL130592 / OLT-22-002465).
Units on cleared permits equal 22–62% of CMHC completions each year 2002–2024 (correlation 0.23). The data has no 2007 clearances and a 2025 batch-closure spike.

Development Applications show current status only: 20–29% of 2020–2025 rezoning files show an appeal state, but only 0–5% of 2008–2015 files. There is no open OLT dataset; Case Status keeps cases two years after closure. Committee of Adjustment appeals are open (Toronto Local Appeal Body (TLAB) data, from 2017).

limitations.lead: Application → permit links exist only for large Planning-Act projects.
limitations.body: The Development Pipeline links them for projects at or above the Site Plan threshold ("fewer than 10 units" are excluded). Its Application Number matches 96.9% of application records, and 98% of "Built" projects match a permit address. It has no permit IDs and no built dates. Everything else links by address.
Among 2018–2025 new-residential permits, 87% of 50+ unit projects are rezoning-linked, and 72–79% of 1–4 unit projects are linked to a minor variance (upper bounds).
DWELLING_UNITS_LOST is filled on about 35% of permits, and the fill rate rises over time.

verdict_conditions.body: Zoning-as-of-date is reconstructable only for 569-2013 lands from 2013 onward, by backcasting. Former-by-law lands are excluded or hand-coded; they hold about half of large-project sites. Report the excluded share in every table.

verdict_conditions.lead: Completions below city level end in 2022.
verdict_conditions.body: Post-2022 analysis uses starts by tract or project-level Pipeline "Built" (undated). Permit clearance is never used as completion.

verdict_conditions.lead: Appeals cannot be measured from open data for older cohorts.
verdict_conditions.body: The appeal analysis is a hand-coded sample of OLT decisions, done by manual lookup.
Rezoning, minor variance and as-of-right are reported separately. As-of-right new construction is a minority in every size class.
Demolition-unit capture improves over time, so net series must be flagged or restricted to recent years. The 2026 Census will provide a net check (counts due 2027, UNVERIFIED).
Built GFA and existing units are estimated from massing heights and the Census.

phase1.fallback: Fallback if Phase 2 finds the backcast unreliable: drop as-of-date capacity. Run (a) a Pipeline cohort study of attrition and stage reached, by Official Plan designation, Secondary Plan or SASP, and (b) a census-tract panel (2010–2022 completions; 2010–2025 starts) on current zoning, with exposure measured only for tracts whose exceptions have no post-2013 amendments.

sub: cohorts 2013-05-09 to 2017, with outcomes to 2022 (census-tract completions);
an extension to 2025 using permits and census-tract starts;
a multiplex marker window around 2023-05-10. New 2–6 unit permits went from 47 in 2022 to 243 in 2025.

frame.html: Unit of analysis: address/parcel for timing and attrition; 2021 census tract for completions.

corrections.html: 3D Massing heights are AVG_HEIGHT/MAX_HEIGHT, not elez. Annual vintages exist for 2016–2023 and 2025.
Open GIS layers exist for Secondary Plans (2015 vintage) and SASPs (Dec 2025).
The Development Pipeline is an open dataset; Active merges three stages.
The holding and exception field names are ZN_HOLDING/HOLDING_ID/ZN_EXCPTN/EXCPTN_NO (now verified).
The Height Overlay field is HT_LABEL, not HT_HEIGHT as the readme says.

unverified.html: Bill 23 and Bill 185 royal assent dates (2022-11-28; 2024-06-06).
The in-force dates of the multiplex (2023-05-12) and garden-suite (2022-07-04) by-laws.
StatCan Census fields and release dates.
The geography of CMHC's conversions and demolitions tables.
Whether files from before 2023 can be retrieved from the Wayback Machine.

files.html: inventory.csv: 30 sources, with fields, coverage, limitations, join keys and provenance.
feasibility.md: definitions, verification, gate answers and verdict.
scripts/: profiling and linkage code. Data is not committed.

gate.q: Q1. Can zoning be obtained as of each application date?
Q2. Is there a project-level link between applications and permits?
gate.a: Yes for Planning-Act projects; by address for the rest.

gate.q: Q3. Is there a completions measure finer than the whole city?
Q4. Years with consistent coverage across all four stages; recommended period.
Q5. Finest reliable unit of analysis.

phase1.overlap: The overlap of all four stages at sub-city level is 2013-05 to 2022-12, about 9.5 years.

inventory.dataset: Building Permits - Cleared Permits (resources: Cleared Building Permits since 2017; Cleared Permits 2000 to 2016)
inventory.license_access: Open Government Licence - Toronto (licence_title on CKAN record; licence text opened at https://open.toronto.ca/open-data-licence/)
inventory.temporal_coverage: COMPLETED_DATE 2001-01-01 to 2026 (2000-2016 file: 448,093 rows; since-2017 file: 447,644 rows). No rows have COMPLETED_DATE in calendar 2007. Publisher note: 'Information for applications where APPLICATION_DATE is earlier than Oct 1, 1999 is likely to be incomplete'
inventory.key_fields: PERMIT_NUM ('Last two digits of calendar year, plus IBMS-generated sequence'); REVISION_NUM; PERMIT_TYPE; STRUCTURE_TYPE; WORK; STREET_NUM; STREET_NAME; STREET_TYPE; STREET_DIRECTION; POSTAL ('First 3 digits'); GEO_ID ('City-defined, unique identifier for Property Address'); WARD_GRID; APPLICATION_DATE; ISSUED_DATE; COMPLETED_DATE ('Date work is complete and permit is cleared'); STATUS; DESCRIPTION; CURRENT_USE; PROPOSED_USE; DWELLING_UNITS_CREATED; DWELLING_UNITS_LOST; EST_CONST_COST; RESIDENTIAL (sq m); DEMOLITION (sq m); BUILDER_NAME (since-2017 file only)
inventory.limitations: No planning-application number. STATUS includes 'Closed' (815,694), 'Cancelled' (62,112) and 'Closed - Dormant' (14,501), so clearance is partly administrative. Units on cleared New Building permits equal 22-62% of CMHC completions each year 2002-2024 (corr 0.23), then surge to 22,359 in 2025 (a batch closure). Only 48% of 50+ unit permits issued 2010-2018 have cleared. DWELLING_UNITS_LOST is non-null for only ~35% of rows; 1 unit record of 100,000 (data error); 11 negative values. The pre-2017 file uses lower-case headers with a timestamp date format.
inventory.join_keys: GEO_ID = Address Points ADDRESS_POINT_ID (88.6% of all permits, 69.8% of new-residential permits). Permit-number stem (first two tokens) groups BLD/Bnn/FND/SHO/STR/PLB/HVA/DRN permits into one folder. Address string -> D04/D05/D06.
inventory.provenance: opened and verified (CKAN package_show + datastore schema via API; full file downloaded and profiled 2026-10-30)

inventory.dataset: Development Applications
inventory.license_access: Open Government Licence - Toronto (licence_title on CKAN record; licence text opened at https://open.toronto.ca/open-data-licence/)
inventory.geographic_coverage: City of Toronto; one row per application-address (26,648 rows; 8,622 unique APPLICATION#)
inventory.temporal_coverage: DATE_SUBMITTED 2008-01-04 to 2026-10-02. Types OZ, SA, SB, PL, CD (no MV/CO). 2,677 unique OZ applications 2008-2025.
inventory.key_fields: APPLICATION_TYPE; APPLICATION#; STREET_NUM/NAME/TYPE/DIRECTION; POSTAL; DATE_SUBMITTED; STATUS ('The internal status of the application in the review process'); X; Y ('The NAD27 x coordinate'); DESCRIPTION; REFERENCE_FILE#; FOLDERRSN; WARD_NUMBER; WARD_NAME; COMMUNITY_MEETING_DATE; APPLICATION_URL; PARENT_FOLDER_NUMBER; CONTACT_* (personal planner contacts; do not republish)
inventory.limitations: Current status only; no decision, approval or appeal dates. STATUS values include Closed, Under Review, 'OMB Appeal' (697 rows), 'OMB Approved', 'Appeal Received' and 'Council Approved'. Appeal status is overwritten once a file closes: only 0-5% of 2008-2015 OZ files show an appeal status, versus 20-29% of 2020-2025 files. Status strings carry trailing spaces. The coordinate CRS label (NAD27) conflicts with value ranges (X 293,785-647,028); verify the CRS.
inventory.join_keys: APPLICATION# = D04 'Application Number' (96.9% match); address -> permits (89-97% of OZ files match some permit address); PARENT_FOLDER_NUMBER links related apps
inventory.provenance: opened and verified (CKAN package_show + datastore schema via API; full file downloaded and profiled 2026-10-30)

inventory.dataset: Development Pipeline
inventory.publisher: City of Toronto - City Planning (Planning Research and Analytics); source Land Use Information System II
inventory.license_access: Open Government Licence - Toronto (licence_title on CKAN record; licence text opened at https://open.toronto.ca/open-data-licence/)
inventory.geographic_coverage: City of Toronto; 2,391 projects; address + ward (no coordinates - publisher: dataset can be geocoded using its addresses)
inventory.temporal_coverage: Rolling five-year window ('projects with activity between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2025' for the 2025 edition); Date Received 1995-2026
inventory.key_fields: 'Pipeline Status' (Under Review 655 / Active 1,089 / Built 647); 'Application Number' (lead application: 1,644 OZ, 744 SA); 'Date Received'; 'Description'; 'Address'; 'Ward'; 'Proposed Residential Gross Floor Area'; 'Proposed Non-Residential Gross Floor Area'; 'Proposed Gross Floor Area'; 'Proposed Residential Units'
inventory.limitations: No Built or permit dates, and no permit numbers. 'Active' merges the bulletin's Approved, Permit Application and Permit Issued stages. Excludes as-of-right work and projects under the Site Plan Control threshold ('fewer than 10 units'). Units are proposed, not as built. Open-data total (927,532 units) differs from the 2025 bulletin (>791,000). 'Built' totals 124,326 units vs. 95,701 CMHC completions in the City 2021-2025, so definitions differ. 'Built' means 'Projects that became ready for occupancy and/or were completed'.
inventory.join_keys: Application Number -> D03 APPLICATION#; Address -> permits (98% of Built projects match a permit address; 79.5% of residential Built projects match a new-residential permit address)
inventory.provenance: opened and verified (CKAN package_show + datastore schema via API; full file downloaded and profiled 2026-10-30); definitions from 2025 bulletin PDF opened

inventory.dataset: Committee of Adjustment Applications
inventory.license_access: Open Government Licence - Toronto (licence_title on CKAN record; licence text opened at https://open.toronto.ca/open-data-licence/)
inventory.temporal_coverage: Closed files 2001-2016 (one resource per closing year) + Closed since 2017 (34,123 rows) + Active (2,789)
inventory.key_fields: SYS_ID; APPLICATION_TYPE (MV/CO); IN_DATE; REFERENCE_FILE#; SUB_TYPE; WORK_TYPE; ZONING_REVIEW; ZONING_DESIGNATION (zone string at application, e.g. 'RD (f9.0; d0.6) (x1249)(ZAP)'); HEARING_DATE; C_OF_A_DESCISION; APPEAL_EXPIRY_DATE; OMB_ORDER_DATE; OMB_DESCISION; NUMBER_OF_LOTS_CREATED; STATUSDESC; FINALDATE; PARENT_FOLDER_NUMBER
inventory.limitations: Field names misspelled at source (DESCISION). Decision text is not standardized ('Approved', 'Approved on condition', etc.). Only 512 rows have OMB_DESCISION. Schemas differ slightly between resources. ZONING_DESIGNATION is free text but records the zoning in force at application date for MV/CO files.
inventory.provenance: opened and verified (CKAN package_show + datastore schema via API; full file downloaded and profiled 2026-10-30)

inventory.dataset: Zoning By-law (569-2013 GIS layers: Zoning Area + 10 overlays + readme)
inventory.license_access: Open Government Licence - Toronto (licence_title on CKAN record; licence text opened at https://open.toronto.ca/open-data-licence/)
inventory.geographic_coverage: Lands subject to 569-2013 only (11,719 Zoning Area polygons). Lands still under former by-laws are absent (no ZN_STATUS=5 polygons in the current file).
inventory.temporal_coverage: Current snapshot. Description: 'updated to include amendments up to June 18th, 2023'. The legal office consolidation runs further ahead (site-specific amendments to July 31, 2024; city-wide to April 30, 2026).
inventory.key_fields: Zoning Area: GEN_ZONE; ZN_ZONE; ZN_HOLDING; HOLDING_ID; FRONTAGE; ZN_AREA; UNITS; DENSITY; COVERAGE; FSI_TOTAL; PRCNT_COMM; PRCNT_RES; PRCNT_EMMP; PRCNT_OFFC; ZN_EXCPTN; EXCPTN_NO; STAND_SET; ZN_STATUS; ZN_STRING; AREA_UNITS; ZBL_CHAPT; ZBL_SECTN; ZBL_EXCPTN. Height Overlay: HT_STORIES; HT_STRING; HT_LABEL (readme says HT_HEIGHT). Lot Coverage: PRCNT_CVER
inventory.limitations: Publisher: 'without direct access to the text of the Zoning By-law, the mapped data is meaningless'. 75.5% of polygons have an exception (ZN_EXCPTN=Y); only 48 have a holding symbol. FSI_TOTAL>0 in only 24.1% of polygons and DENSITY>0 in 18.7%. 50.8% of 50+ unit new-building permits (and 12.7% of single-unit ones) geocode outside any 569-2013 polygon. No version history; Wayback Machine holds CKAN copies captured 2023-04-04 and 2024-06-05.
inventory.join_keys: Spatial (EPSG:2952) via Address Points; EXCPTN_NO + zone -> Chapter 900 exception text (D08)
inventory.provenance: opened and verified (CKAN package_show + datastore schema via API; full file downloaded and profiled 2026-10-30); readme downloaded; spatial join run

phase2.intro: Code scaffolding for studying how zoning relates to development applications, permits and completed housing in Toronto. It has only been run on synthetic data. No real Toronto data is loaded, and nothing here describes Toronto; the loaders are deliberately unfilled until the field names are confirmed from verified data dictionaries (Phase 1 output).

rows: Canonical tables (applications, permits, zoning_versions, parcels) and validation
Map raw columns onto the canonical schema; refuses to run with an unfilled mapping
Chain permits into projects; one-to-one link of applications to projects; match diagnostics
Zoning in force as of a date; check whether history exists; crude zoned capacity
Per-application pipeline table, cohort funnel, time-to-event inputs
Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence (competing risks), Kaplan-Meier, bootstrap CI
Compare project-level completions with an aggregate series (e.g. CMHC)
Synthetic data with a known ground truth, for testing
run() wires the steps together; CLI runs the synthetic check

design.html: Zoning as of the application date, never today's zoning. history_coverage tells you whether the zoning table has any history; if not, the join degenerates into a snapshot.

Rezoning is separated from as-of-right via requires_rezoning, because applications are selected on zoning not permitting what the developer wants. An unlinked project is not necessarily as-of-right; it may be a failed link.
Permits are aggregated to projects; a project is complete only when all observed permits are cleared. Unit counts use max by default to avoid double-counting repeated units.

Completion rates use cumulative incidence, not shares. Recent cohorts have not had time to complete; the naive share is biased low (the synthetic run shows this), and treating refusals as censoring would bias the other way.

phase2.assumptions: permit_chain_gap_days, link_before_days, link_max_lag_days, unit_agg, avg_unit_floor_area_m2, residential_efficiency. data_end must be the date the sources are complete through, not the download date.

limitations.html: Link failures look like non-completion: unlinked approved applications stay censored forever, biasing completion low. Watch share_approved_apps_linked.
Approved projects that silently die are invisible without a cancellation record.
Refused/withdrawn applications with no decision date are treated as censored (flagged in competing_missing_date), which biases completion high.
Existing floor area is normally a current snapshot, so it understates unbuilt capacity for past applications. Zoned capacity from floor-area ratio alone is an upper bound.
Independent censoring requires stable timelines across calendar time; compare cohorts and policy periods rather than only pooling. Bootstrap intervals ignore spatial clustering.
The synthetic test shows the estimators work when the assumptions hold. It says nothing about how well they hold in real data.

next_steps.html: Fill loaders.mapping_template for each verified dataset; recode categorical values.
Run history_coverage on the zoning table (the Phase 1 feasibility question).
Choose data_end, the unit of analysis, and a study period; re-check the config assumptions.
Run reconcile_with_aggregate against the completions series before trusting permit clearance as a completion measure.

audit_fixed.html: Refused/withdrawn applications with no decision date were silently censored, overstating completion. Now flagged (competing_missing_date) and reported by run().

requires_rezoning given as strings silently made every route unknown, and a pandas nullable-boolean column would crash np.select. Now normalized to nullable boolean in validate (strings are rejected) and the route logic is NA-safe.
run() did not report a parcel match rate. Added parcel_match_rate.

audit_checks.html: Tests pass from the repo root and from phase2/, with -W error, and on pandas 2.2.3 as well as the newest pandas (the geopandas test skips when geopandas is absent).

Mutation checks (10 injected bugs in a scratch copy). Two survived at first and led to new tests: signed-vs-absolute lag in greedy linking (the old test used only positive lags), and the precedence of a completed project over a refusal in the missing-date flag. All 10 are now caught.

phase2.audit_not_covered: Not covered: the code has never touched real data, so field names, join keys and the realism of every default in config.py are untested.

ideas.caveat: Under-studied angles, picked because they are awkward to measure or fall between disciplines. Data sources are suggestions and still need to be verified before relying on them.

items.name: Street-name demographics
items.question: Who do streets honor (gender, race, era, colonial or Confederate figures), and how do renaming debates play out?
items.data: OpenStreetMap street names plus public biographical records

items.name: Who gets to sit down?
items.question: How much public seating is there per capita and along walking routes, and how does it vary with age, disability, and income?
items.data: OpenStreetMap, city asset inventories, a field audit

items.name: Geography of waiting
items.question: Where do people wait for buses, benefits, and clinics, and what do those spots offer (shelter, shade, seating, safety)?
items.data: Transit stop data (GTFS), city facility lists, field observation

items.name: Soundscape and gentrification
items.question: How does what a neighborhood sounds like change as it changes (construction, vendors, bells, children)?

items.name: Urban smell mapping
items.question: who lives with sewage, rendering plants, or cannabis odors, and who gets to complain?

items.name: Nighttime cities
items.question: lighting, night-shift transit access, and how safe the night feels by neighborhood.

items.name: Death and the city
items.question: cemetery land use, cremation trends, and roadside memorials.

items.name: Ghost infrastructure
items.question: unfinished highways, closed stations, and orphaned plazas. What predicts failure, and does reuse work?

items.name: Urban wildlife as a stakeholder
items.question: camera-trap and community-science data (iNaturalist) across income lines.

items.name: Informal city in rich countries
items.question: unpermitted units, garage conversions, street vending, ad-hoc parking markets.

items.name: Elevators and the vertical city
items.question: subway elevator outages and who is trapped when they fail.

items.name: Loneliness geography
items.question: free places to be alone or together (libraries, plazas, laundromats) against indicators of isolation.

items.name: Delivery-economy footprints
items.question: how ghost kitchens, dark stores, and delivery bikes reshape curbs and commercial streets.

items.name: Teenagers and the city
items.question: where 13-18-year-olds can legally hang out, and what happens when they cannot.

items.name: Transit access vs. home values
items.question: distance to stations against census-tract home values, using a new line as a natural experiment. Property-level sales data (TRREB) and bulk assessment data (MPAC) are licensed, so aggregates and census data are the realistic route.

items.name: Multiplex reform as a natural experiment
items.question: did permitting rules allowing multiplexes citywide change what gets built? This pairs naturally with the Phase 2 pipeline below.

items.name: Downtown recovery
items.question: foot traffic across cities and what explains the differences.

items.name: Legacy of redlining
items.question: historical maps against today's health, wealth, and environmental burdens.

items.name: Heat-island equity
items.question: tree canopy and surface materials against heat-related ER visits, by income and race.
